'''Isador Mitchell Sheffer''' (October 15, 1901&ndash;April 20, 1992) was an American [[mathematician]] best known for the [[Sheffer sequence]] of polynomials.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Boas | first1 = R. P. Jr. |author-link=Ralph P. Boas Jr.
 | last2 = Buck | first2 = R. C.
 | doi = 10.2307/2310587
 | journal = The American Mathematical Monthly
 | mr = 0080777
 | pages = 626–632
 | title = Polynomials defined by generating relations
 | volume = 63
 | year = 1956}}.</ref> Born in [[Massachusetts]], he lived a large portion of his life in [[State College, Pennsylvania]], where he was a Professor of Mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].

He received his PhD from [[Harvard University]] in 1927, under the direction of [[George Birkhoff]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|4947}}</ref>
